```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE,
                      comment = "#>", fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6,
                      dpi = 150, out.width = "100%")
library(spatialGPCA)
library(ggplot2)
output <- Sys.getenv("SPATIALGPCA_FULL_OUTPUT",
                     unset = file.path(tempdir(), "spatialGPCA_full_fit"))
dir.create(output, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
mm <- if (requireNamespace("CppMatrix", quietly = TRUE)) CppMatrix::matrixMultiply else `%*%`
```

This is a complete **synthetic SPDE BED fit**, including smoothing-parameter selection,
spatial PCs and SNP-specific fitted geographic effects. All 150,000 SNPs enter
the fit. There are 3,000 distinct Lat/Lon locations. An independent RTriangle mesh
is constructed entirely through the package's public functions. Multiple individuals
share each location. These are simulated US coordinates and genotypes, not real
genetic records.

The simulation plants three smooth spatial fields and independent binomial
genotype draws conditional on the fields and fixed effects. This is a recovery
demonstration using the package's Gaussian working model for standardized means.

## Individual table and known geographic signal

Every column after FID, IID, Lat, Lon is a location-level fixed effect, repeated
for individuals at that location. Location counts are derived by the package.

```{r simulate-locations}
set.seed(1909)
nloc <- 3000L
p <- 150000L
lon <- runif(30000, -124, -67)
lat <- runif(30000, 25, 49)
inside <- !is.na(maps::map.where("state", lon, lat))
ll <- data.frame(Lat = lat[inside][seq_len(nloc)], Lon = lon[inside][seq_len(nloc)])
Ni <- sample(2:4, nloc, replace = TRUE)
loc <- rep(seq_len(nloc), Ni)
n <- length(loc)
C <- data.frame(GPC1 = rnorm(nloc), GPC2 = rnorm(nloc),
                urban = as.numeric(ll$Lat > 38), income = rnorm(nloc, 50000, 12000))
table <- data.frame(FID = sprintf("F%06d", seq_len(n)),
                    IID = sprintf("I%06d", seq_len(n)),
                    Lat = ll$Lat[loc], Lon = ll$Lon[loc], C[loc, ])
rownames(table) <- NULL
X <- cbind(1, as.matrix(C))
qX <- qr(X * sqrt(Ni))
H <- cbind(sin((ll$Lon + 100) / 8), cos((ll$Lat - 36) / 4),
           exp(-((ll$Lon + 85) / 9)^2 - ((ll$Lat - 34) / 6)^2))
H <- qr.resid(qX, H * sqrt(Ni)) / sqrt(Ni)
H <- sweep(H, 2, apply(abs(H), 2, max), "/")
Z <- scale(as.matrix(C))
Z <- sweep(Z, 2, apply(abs(Z), 2, max), "/")
head(table)
```

The regression residual above defines the **simulation truth** so that its
spatial fields are weighted-orthogonal to the intercept and all fixed effects.
It does not replace the package's spatial-basis QR calculation.

## Generate BED and allele frequencies in blocks

No full individual-by-SNP or location-by-SNP matrix is created. SNPs have
independent random loadings on the three spatial fields, small fixed effects,
and 1.5% missing genotype calls. Bounds on these loadings keep all simulated
allele probabilities strictly between zero and one, without clipping.

```{r simulate-bed}
prefix <- file.path(output, "us_genotypes")
fam <- data.frame(table[, 1:2], father = 0, mother = 0, sex = 0, phenotype = -9)
bim <- data.frame(CHROM = 1, ID = paste0("rs", seq_len(p)),
                  CM = 0, POS = seq_len(p), A1 = "A", A2 = "C")
write.table(fam, paste0(prefix, ".fam"), row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
write.table(bim, paste0(prefix, ".bim"), row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
af <- obs <- numeric(p)
missing_calls <- 0
Y4 <- truth4 <- matrix(0, nloc, 4)
con <- file(paste0(prefix, ".bed"), "wb")
writeBin(as.raw(c(0x6c, 0x1b, 1)), con)
    for (start in seq(1L, p, by = 256L)) {
        j <- start:min(p, start + 255L)
        f <- runif(length(j), .25, .45)
        b <- matrix(runif(3 * length(j), -.04, .04), 3)
        a <- matrix(runif(4 * length(j), -.005, .005), 4)
        S <- mm(H, b)
        prob <- sweep(S + mm(Z, a), 2, f, "+")
        G <- matrix(rbinom(n * length(j), 2, prob[loc, ]), n)
        G[runif(length(G)) < .015] <- NA
        obs[j] <- 2 * colSums(!is.na(G))
        af[j] <- colSums(G, na.rm = TRUE) / obs[j]
        missing_calls <- missing_calls + sum(is.na(G))
        if (start == 1L) {
            for (k in 1:4) {
                g <- G[, k]
                g[is.na(g)] <- 2 * af[k]
                Y4[, k] <- (rowsum(g, loc)[, 1] / Ni - 2 * af[k]) /
                            sqrt(2 * af[k] * (1 - af[k]))
                truth4[, k] <- 2 * S[, k] / sqrt(2 * af[k] * (1 - af[k]))
            }
        }
        for (k in seq_along(j)) {
            codes <- c(3L, 2L, 0L)[G[, k] + 1L]
            codes[is.na(codes)] <- 1L
            length(codes) <- ceiling(n / 4) * 4
            codes[is.na(codes)] <- 0L
            writeBin(as.raw(colSums(matrix(codes, 4) * c(1L, 4L, 16L, 64L))), con)
        }
    }
close(con)
ff <- data.frame(CHROM = 1, ID = bim$ID, REF = "C", ALT = "A", ALT_FREQS = af,
                 OBS_CT = obs, check.names = FALSE)
names(ff)[1] <- "#CHROM"
write.table(ff, paste0(prefix, ".afreq"), row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t")
data.frame(individuals = n, locations = nloc, SNPs = p, missing_calls = missing_calls,
           BED_MiB = file.info(paste0(prefix, ".bed"))$size / 2^20)
```

G counts BIM allele A1 = A. The `.afreq` has ALT = A, REF = C and the observed
frequency of A, with ordinary PLINK2 column names. This simulation writes that
file itself; it does not claim to execute PLINK2. For real data, use the existing
BED and `plink2 --bfile merged --freq --out merged` output directly.

## Construct and inspect the SPDE mesh

We shuffle the table to exercise FAM matching during fitting. Mesh construction
uses the geographic table and does not require BED or GP clustering.

```{r mesh}
table <- table[sample(nrow(table)), ]
locations <- svgpc_spde_locations(table)
mesh <- svgpc_spde_mesh(locations, max_area = 8000, buffer = 150)
mesh
png(file.path(output, "us_mesh.png"), width = 1600, height = 900, res = 160)
plot(mesh)
points(locations$locations[, c("x", "y")], pch = 16, cex = .25, col = "#C76A36")
invisible(dev.off())
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(output, "us_mesh.png"))
```

Orange points are the observation locations; mesh vertices are the SPDE knots.
The maximum triangle area is 8,000 km² and the rectangular boundary extends
150 km beyond the study bounds. The mesh is not clipped to coastlines.
These are illustrative choices; check mesh resolution and buffer for your study.

## Fit every SNP and obtain spatial PCs

```{r fit}
scale <- svgpc_spde_scale(distance = 150)
model <- svgpc_spde_prepare_data(mesh, table, kappa = scale$kappa, bed = prefix)
model <- svgpc_spde_accumulate(model, paste0(prefix, ".afreq"))
parameters <- svgpc_spde_select_lambda(model, method = "REML")
result <- svgpc_spde_fit(model, parameters = parameters, components = 10)
PC <- result$outputs$raw_F_PCA$pcs
locations <- model$spatial$locations
parameters
```

The scale sets nominal Matérn correlation exp(-1) at 150 km, independently of
mesh resolution. One genotype-based lambda is estimated and reused for PCA.
No 150,000 by 150,000
matrix is formed. BED accumulation uses the default 256-SNP blocks, with 2f
imputation, location averaging, centering, scaling and sample-count weights.

## Geographic distribution of the fitted PCs

These are **fitted PC scores at each of the 3,000 locations**, not cluster labels.
PC signs are arbitrary. Each panel has its own symmetric colour scale after
division by its maximum absolute score; the saved PC matrix is unchanged.

```{r pc-map, fig.height=8}
outline <- ggplot2::map_data("state")
Pdat <- data.frame(Lon = rep(locations$Lon, 4), Lat = rep(locations$Lat, 4),
                   PC = rep(paste0("Spatial PC ", 1:4), each = nloc),
                   score = as.vector(sweep(PC[, 1:4], 2, apply(abs(PC[, 1:4]), 2, max), "/")))
Ppc <- ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = outline, aes(long, lat, group = group),
                 fill = "#F1F3F5", colour = "#B3BDC5", linewidth = .15) +
    geom_point(data = Pdat, aes(Lon, Lat, colour = score), size = .55, stroke = 0) +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#B2182B",
                           limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Relative score") +
    facet_wrap(~PC, ncol = 2) + coord_quickmap(xlim = c(-125, -66), ylim = c(24, 50)) +
    labs(title = "SPDE spatial PCs: 150,000 SNPs, 3,000 locations", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
Ppc
ggsave(file.path(output, "spatial_pcs.png"), Ppc, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 160)
```

## Recovery of the planted spatial subspace

We compare the span of the three planted fields with the first three fitted
PCs using canonical correlations. This comparison allows arbitrary signs and
rotations; it does not require PC 1 to be the first simulated field.

```{r recovery}
Q <- qr.Q(qr(H))
cs <- svd(crossprod(Q, PC[, 1:3]), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d
recovery <- data.frame(direction = 1:3, canonical_correlation = cs,
                       angle_degrees = acos(pmin(1, cs)) * 180 / pi)
recovery
```

## SNP-specific geographic effects

The first four SNPs were selected before fitting. `svgpc_spde_fitted()` takes their
standardized location means and the already selected lambda to obtain
posterior fitted geographic effects; it does not fit another lambda. Fixed
effects are excluded from the returned geographic component.

```{r geographic-effects}
Fhat <- svgpc_spde_fitted(model, Y4, lambda = parameters$lambda)
effects <- data.frame(SNP = paste0("rs", 1:4),
                      correlation = diag(cor(truth4, Fhat)),
                      RMSE = sqrt(colMeans((truth4 - Fhat)^2)))
effects
```

The truth here is the planted geographic contribution in standardized genotype
units before missing-call imputation. With finite individual counts and missing
calls, a fitted field need not equal its truth. Both rows below use the same
colour scale, so amplitude shrinkage remains visible.

```{r effect-map, fig.height=7}
Edat <- data.frame(Lon = rep(ll$Lon, 8), Lat = rep(ll$Lat, 8),
                   SNP = rep(rep(paste0("rs", 1:4), each = nloc), 2),
                   source = factor(rep(c("Simulated geographic effect", "Fitted geographic effect"),
                                       each = nloc * 4),
                                   levels = c("Simulated geographic effect", "Fitted geographic effect")),
                   effect = c(as.vector(truth4), as.vector(Fhat)))
lim <- max(abs(Edat$effect))
Pe <- ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = outline, aes(long, lat, group = group),
                 fill = "#F1F3F5", colour = "#B3BDC5", linewidth = .15) +
    geom_point(data = Edat, aes(Lon, Lat, colour = effect), size = .4, stroke = 0) +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#B2182B",
                           limits = c(-lim, lim), name = "Standardized effect") +
    facet_grid(source ~ SNP) + coord_quickmap(xlim = c(-125, -66), ylim = c(24, 50)) +
    labs(title = "Known and fitted SNP geographic effects", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
Pe
ggsave(file.path(output, "geographic_effects.png"), Pe, width = 13, height = 7, dpi = 160)
```

## Save the fitted results

```{r save}
saveRDS(list(result = result, locations = locations), file.path(output, "result.rds"))
write.table(cbind(locations[, c("Lat", "Lon", "count")], PC),
            file.path(output, "spatial_pcs.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

The result contains the spatial PC subspace and its location metadata.
`Fhat` contains the four SNP-specific geographic effects. The simulation data
and output files are written under `SPATIALGPCA_FULL_OUTPUT` when that
environment variable is set, otherwise under the R temporary directory.
